findings.question: sensible
findings.text: The approach solves the stated problem: the escalation ladder currently skips two tiers upstream already publishes. The problem belongs in the skills district, where book-index.md already lives, not in a new seam.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.constraint_introduced: A design or review-mode session must load a minimum of three nano-tier book excerpts before it may escalate any one book to mini or full tier. Full-tier loading is judgment-gated per book, never unconditional.
findings.text: This establishes a real invariant on book-index.md's own escalation rule, replacing the prior 1-primary-plus-1-companion cap for book loading specifically.

findings.question: new_pattern_or_duplicate
findings.text: No ADR or existing file in docs/architecture/adr/ or inventory.yaml covers tiered reference-doc escalation today. This is a new pattern for this repo, not a duplicate or reinvention.

regret_risk: Judgment-gated escalation has no mechanical check. This repo's own CLAUDE.md names exactly this failure mode from the Gate 4b history: a process step with no mechanical consumer gets skipped, however well it is documented. If that happens here, the 42-file vendoring cost is paid while sessions silently keep reading only full, the same as today, and the nano/mini tiers sit unread.
